title: Dedicated capacity throughput measurement harness and customer acceptance tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible load-testing and benchmarking harness for Dedicated capacity that validates contractual throughput guarantees, verifies autoscaling policy behavior, and produces customer acceptance test (CAT) artifacts. The harness must support trace replay of customer traffic shapes, synthetic workload templates (steady, ramp, burst), cache-warm vs cache-cold scenarios, configurable batching and sequence length distributions, and multiple model/quantization variants. Output should include a machine-readable report, Grafana dashboard links, and a runbook checklist for on-call engineers and SEs running CATs with customers.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay stored customer request traces with preserved inter-arrival distribution and token lengths
Sustained throughput test: system sustains committed QPS for 30 minutes with p95 latency <= 250ms and error rate <= 0.5% under configured model/runtime settings
Burst handling: when injected load spikes to 2x committed QPS for 2 minutes, autoscaling actions trigger within configured policy window and overall error rate remains <= 1%
Cache-warm vs cache-cold: measurable delta reported between cold-start and warmed-KV-cache throughput/latency; documentation produced for expected warmup time
Multi-tenant isolation scenario shows no degradation beyond 5% for co-located tenants under simulated noisy neighbor workload
Automated report (JSON + HTML) produced after each run summarizing key metrics and flags for failed thresholds
SE-run CAT checklist validated in two pilot customer runs and signed off by support and product engineering
implementation_steps: Design harness API and CLI: inputs (trace file, template, model config), outputs (report, metrics tags)
Prototype traffic generator using k6 for HTTP-level scenarios and a lightweight custom gRPC generator for internal protocol paths
Add trace-replay support: time-shifted replay preserving per-request metadata and optional anonymization
Implement workload templates: steady-state, linear-ramp, sudden-burst, poisson-arrival, long-tail token distributions
Instrument test runner to emit Prometheus-compatible metrics with labels for run_id, customer_id, model, region, and batch_size
Integrate with autoscaling simulation hooks: ability to toggle real autoscaler vs dry-run mode and capture scaling events
Create standardized dashboard panels (Grafana) and report generator (JSON + human-readable HTML) with pass/fail summary
Write CAT runbook and checklist for SEs including pre-tests, warmup, acceptance validation, and post-test cleanup
Run two internal pilot CATs with synthetic tenants and iterate on thresholds and time windows
Ship harness and docs; create onboarding PR and notify SELL/CS teams
test_scenarios: Cold-start full-cluster: bring nodes online and run ramp to target QPS measuring warmup behavior
Warm-cache steady-state: populate KV cache then sustain target QPS for 30+ minutes
Burst spike: 2x QPS for 2 minutes then return to baseline
Gradual ramp: linear increase to 100% over 10 minutes
Tail-heavy: 5% of requests with long sequences (>2x median tokens) to validate latency tail behavior
Autoscaler policy validation: run in policy-observed mode to check scale out/in timing and overshoot
instrumentation: Prometheus scrape of service metrics + node exporter for GPU/CPU/memory
Tracing (Jaeger) for sampled requests to inspect end-to-end latency breakdown
Log annotations for test run_id and customer_id to correlate errors with harness actions
Synthetic request headers to mark cache-control and routing policies
Dashboard templates (Grafana) with exportable share links included in report
notes: We intentionally separate HTTP-level and internal RPC generators to keep test surface close to customer integration paths
Default p95 threshold chosen conservatively for initial pilots; we expect to tighten to 200ms after kernel-level optimizations land
Privacy: trace replay supports anonymization; CATs with real customer data must be run under signed data handling agreement
Autoscaling dry-run mode records what actions would have been taken without mutating live config to allow safe validation
